business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Automated Dropshipping Networks

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (federal common law and Quebec civil law under the Civil Code of Quebec)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada–Republic of Korea Free Trade Agreement
Canada–United States Income Tax Convention (1980), as amended

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, and associated FINTRAC regulations under SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Part XII.2 (sections 462.3 et seq.); Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, sections 21.1–21.8 (federal register of individuals with significant control); Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, sections 83.1–83.7 (provincial register); Quebec Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1 and its regulations (Registraire des entreprises ultimate-beneficiary declaration; publicly searchable).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of name reservation and Registaire des entreprises excerpts for the proposed corporate name
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic registry certification; no foreign apostille or consular legalization required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled certified copy of each director's and ultimate beneficial owner's passport (or equivalent national identity document) and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for HCCH 1961 member states) or consular legalization by Global Affairs Canada / Canadian embassy or high commission for non-member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Quebec incorporator or registered agent to execute incorporation filings and receive service of process
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country where the appointer signs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization by the competent Canadian diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn declaration of individuals with significant control under Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c S-31.1, sections 83.1–83.7
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notaire du Québec or a foreign notary where a Quebec resident director is not available
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Quebec notarial execution; foreign execution requires Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: KYC/AML clearing certificate from a Canadian Schedule I bank or FINTRAC-regulated financial institution for the corporate opening profile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct bank certification to Revenu Québec, FINTRAC, and pocketing bank; no apostille required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, HM Treasury Consolidated List, and Canadian autonomous sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2011, c. 32, s. 1. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) must be identified in accordance with section 11.1 of the PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for automated dropshipping payment rails, including Stripe and PayPal, and adverse findings require elevated approval and ongoing transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Online Name Reservation Centre (Centre de réservation de nom), https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca; for federal incorporation, Corporations Canada NUANS name reservation portal may alternatively be used, but Quebec enterprise registration will still be required.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, requires that the corporate name be expressed in French. A non-French name, including a transliterated or translated form, may be accepted only where an approved French version is also set out in the articles. Legal suffixes such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.' and 'Ltée' are permitted, and a non-Latin script must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet using generally accepted Quebec transliteration standards.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name reservation is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration request with the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of the notice, accompanied by a revised NUANS or registraire search abstract and, if necessary, a Quebec legal opinion on distinctiveness and compliance with the Charter of the French Language. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may apply to the Superior Court of Quebec for judicial review under articles 34 and 529 of the Code of Civil Procedure, CQLR c C-25.01, within 30 days of notification, or may immediately file a fresh name reservation with an amended corporate name using a separate distinctive token.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable for Quebec registered-office purposes only if the service provider maintains a physical street address in Quebec, is staffed during normal business hours, accepts service of process, and does not operate solely as a post-office box. For an automated dropshipping business, a virtual office alone will not establish Quebec commercial substance for CRA and Revenu Québec purposes; the corporation should maintain local books and records, director/management presence, a local business bank account, and operational contracts demonstrating substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk is low to moderate: approximately 5–10% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection in the first fiscal year for a compliant no-inventory dropshipping entity, increasing to approximately 20–30% if material input tax credits are claimed, related-party cross-border payments arise, or the corporation is flagged by the CRA/Revenu Québec under a corporate-beneficial-ownership verification program.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1, as amended; applicable provisions on constitution, registered office, directors, officers, shares and amendments.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar), Corporate Constitution Service
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (statuts constitutifs) filed electronically with the Registraire des entreprises, evidenced by the certificate of constitution / attestation de constitution
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow or capital deposit account is required under the Quebec Business Corporations Act. The incorporator may subscribe shares, and the board fixes the consideration for issued shares.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The incorporator's subscription for 100 common shares is accepted, and the board hereby issued those shares as fully paid in consideration of the capital contributed. (2) The registered office is established at 1250 Boulevard René-Lévesque, Montréal, QC, and is designated for service under the Business Corporations Act. (3) Jamie Smith is appointed President and Chief Executive Officer, Taylor Lee is appointed Secretary, and Jordan Patel is appointed Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until successors are elected. (4) The board adopts the specimen share certificate and corporate by-laws, and authorizes officers to file all statutory declarations with the Registraire des entreprises. Approved unanimously by written consent this 15th day of April, 2025.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Online Services (Quebec Business Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS-style name search in the Quebec enterprise registry or use an accredited NUANS search house. If conflicting names appear, select a revised distinctive name. If reservation is desired, file a name reservation request with the registrar and obtain the reservation certificate before filing the articles of incorporation.
required_dossiers: NUANS or Quebec name search report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the search reveals a confusingly similar name, file a revised name request or submit a written consent from the conflicting name holder; otherwise the application will be refused.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and legal counsel; form prescribed by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of incorporation in French or English in the prescribed statutory form. Include the corporate name, share classes and terms, restrictions on business, initial registered office address, and first directors. The incorporator must sign the articles and record the date and place of execution.
required_dossiers: Signed consent to act of first directors
Share subscription or statement of consideration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar flags incomplete or inconsistent clauses, submit corrected articles or a written explanation within the stated cure period; no fresh fee applies if the correction is timely made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Online Submission of Articles and Payment of Filing Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Online Transaction Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the online incorporation service, upload the signed articles, complete the statutory filing declaration, pay the applicable tariff, and submit. Retain the electronic acknowledgment; the registrar will issue the certificate of constitution once the file is accepted.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected for incompleteness, correct the flagged data fields and resubmit within the registrar's notice period; a timely revised submission will not attract an additional constitution fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Initial Enterprise Registration and Tax Account Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After constitution, confirm the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) issued by the Registrar. Register the corporation with Revenu Québec and CRA for corporate income tax, GST/HST/QST, payroll deductions and any applicable consumption tax accounts. Update the registry profile with directors, officers, registered office and business activity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If account activation is delayed, contact the CRA or Revenu Québec business line, resubmit the certificate of constitution and provide any missing officer identification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting, By-law Adoption and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or obtain unanimous written consent. Adopt the first board resolution, issue share certificates to the subscriber, approve general by-law No. 1, appoint officers, and authorize banking arrangements. Record all resolutions, share subscriptions, share transfers and consents in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Waiver of notice or meeting notice
Share subscription records and share ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer or director declines to act, convene an immediate board meeting to appoint a replacement and file the revised declaration with the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Statutory Records Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Office in Quebec and Registraire des entreprises du Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the registered office at a physical address in Quebec. Keep the articles, by-laws, resolutions, share records, minutes and accounting records at the registered office or another prescribed location. File annual declarations and any amendments through the Registrar's online portal as required.
required_dossiers: Corporate minute book and statutory records
Annual declaration calendar and registry access credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office changes or a record is incomplete, file the required declaration of amendment promptly and update the minute book to avoid registry penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 4791 automated dropshipping retail; commercial regulatory contact is the Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required; no statutory industry-specific operating, manufacturing or import permit applies to pure automated dropshipping activities.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt; e-commerce and dropshipping is not a listed industrial installation requiring a full EIA report or registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Core activity generates no wastewater, VOC or solid waste discharges. Any warehousing or product-storage operation must comply with municipal wastewater bylaws, RECYC-QUÉBEC packaging recovery obligations and, where applicable, the Quebec Clean Air Regulation for heating, ventilation and refrigeration equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for pure administrative dropshipping. If a physical storage or fulfillment space is used, obtain a local fire safety certificate, structural load inspection under the Quebec Construction Code, and a CNESST occupational health and safety workplace clearance for employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA) — federal income tax, GST/HST, and customs duties portal (My Business Account: https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/services-business/business-account.html); Revenu Québec (RQ) — Quebec provincial income tax, QST, and related levies portal (Clic Revenu: https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/); Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) — customs export declaration and border clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Quebec-registered business corporation (including a foreign-owned Canadian subsidiary) and for a foreign dropshipping principal, the statutory TIN/VAT ID procurement sequence is: (1) incorporate or maintain the CBCA/QBCA corporation and obtain the articles of incorporation and Quebec NEQ (numéro d'entreprise du Québec) from the Registraire des entreprises; (2) obtain the nine-digit federal Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration Online or Form RC1, which automatically creates the RC (corporation income tax) account; (3) open the GST/HST 'RT' program account on the same BN using Form RC1 or the GST/HST account registration service, stating the effective registration date and worldwide taxable supply volumes; (4) register for QST with Revenu Québec (combined federal/provincial registration election available) using the BN-based RQ account and, where applicable, the Quebec enterprise number; (5) appoint a Canadian representative for service if the corporation is a non-resident-owned or non-resident-managed entity without a physical establishment in Canada; (6) retain CRA and RQ certificates, account confirmation numbers, and authorization history as evidence of the statutory tax identity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not offer check-the-box classification; a business corporation is per se an entity-level taxpayer and may not elect pass-through treatment. Available statutory elections and structured arrangements: (i) ETA s. 156 election for closely related corporations to treat intercompany supplies as made for nil consideration for GST/QST purposes; (ii) GST/HST quick-method election for registrants with annual worldwide taxable supplies not exceeding C$400,000 (Form GST74); (iii) ETA s. 177 election on transfers of designated property among registrants; (iv) hybrid mismatch rule disallowances under ITA ss. 18.2-18.6 (BEPS Action 2) that deny deductions for structured payments with deductibility/non-inclusion mismatches; (v) the Quebec combined GST/QST registration and single-return election administered by Revenu Québec.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BOC) as monetary authority; Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as prudential regulator of federally regulated financial institutions; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) as AML/ATF supervisory authority; Revenu Québec for provincial licensing of money services businesses.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. There are no foreign exchange controls, no restrictions on the repatriation of profits, and no requirement for central bank approval on inward or outward remittances. Cross-border transfers equal to or above C$10,000 must be reported to FINTRAC. For dropshipping activities, payments for goods and services fall within the current account and are freely remittable. Dividends to non-resident shareholders are subject to Canadian non-resident withholding tax at treaty rates, but the underlying FX transfer is unrestricted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no mandatory surrender requirements for export proceeds. Dropshipping receipts in foreign currency (e.g., USD) may be retained in foreign-currency bank accounts, converted at commercial rates, or repatriated without a timeline. For statistical purposes, exporters must file a B13A Export Declaration if goods are exported, but for dropshipping where goods ship directly from suppliers (often non-Canadian), the service fee component is not an export of goods. No CAD conversion ratio exists. All records must be kept for tax and AML compliance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Moderate. Canadian-regulated fintechs (e.g., Stripe Treasury, Payoneer, Wise Canada) can operate as payment service providers or money services businesses (MSBs) under FINTRAC and provincial regulations. Foreign offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Revolut) may offer CAD accounts but must be registered as MSBs in Canada if serving Canadian clients. For automated dropshipping with Stripe and PayPal as target rails, such EMIs provide ancillary clearing but cannot replace a Canadian chartered bank for settlement in CAD via the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or Real-Time Rail (RTR). Key legal constraints: MSB registration, beneficial ownership disclosure, and FINTRAC reporting thresholds. EMIs are less viable for capital escrow accounts due to lack of OSFI deposit insurance (CDIC).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate account opening is generally permitted for Canadian directors. For non-resident directors, most Tier-1 banks require a physical interview at a branch or Canadian embassy/consulate, or a notarized document package. National Bank of Canada and RBC allow remote onboarding for non-resident directors with full CDD evidence (certified copies of passports, proof of address, corporate registry extracts). However, for complex beneficial ownership structures, physical presence may be mandated by the bank's AML compliance. Dropshipping entities with no physical office in Quebec face Medium-to-High friction; a registered agent address and a local EPC compliance representative (e.g., in Montreal) materially improve onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Automated dropshipping model with high volume of small transactions from multiple e-commerce platforms (Stripe, PayPal) triggering transaction monitoring alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business narrative explaining cross-border B2B/B2C flow; executed supplier agreements with global warehouses; platform settlement statements (last 6 months); logistics contracts with tracking proof; refund/chargeback policy; projected transaction volume annualized; and a clear organizational chart of the automated order flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity due to non-resident shareholders or nominee directors that complexity the source of funds / wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate register excerpt (Quebec Registraire des entreprises), share register with full legal names and addresses of all BOs, notarized trust agreements or holding company chart, passport copies, source-of-wealth affidavit, and bank reference letters from the jurisdiction of incorporation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume disbursements to overseas suppliers (especially to jurisdictions flagged for counterfeit or sanctioned goods).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier due diligence file with KYC profile of each manufacturer, supplier contracts, commercial invoices, and bill of lading / airway bill evidence, ISO certifications or brand authorizations, and evidence that no transactions occur with prohibited or sanctioned jurisdictions (UN/OFAC/CFSAN screening).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from a foreign parent or related party structured as a loan or equity that may look like a potential money laundering layering step.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized loan or subscription agreement, board resolution authorizing the capital injection, evidence of corporate tax registration in home jurisdiction, source-of-funds statement from the remitting bank, and if convertible, a fair-market valuation report.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant method: international wire transfer via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent or shareholder to the Canadian operational account. Purpose code: In the message field 70 (Remittance Information) use 'Capital contribution – equity subscription' or 'Shareholder loan – intercompany funding' and include the Quebec enterprise registration number. Frequencies above C$10,000 trigger FINTRAC report. For amounts greater than C$100,000, the bank may require evidence of the corporate resolution and beneficial ownership. Funds can be received in CAD, USD, or EUR and converted via the bank's spot rate. The corporate account must be opened before the transfer. Ensure that the receiving bank has a valid correspondent relationship with the remitting bank; avoid using non-bank money transmitters for escrow capital injections.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 (Single Customer Credit Transfer) for standard supplier payments, with a corporate-to-corporate instruction including the supplier's full bank details and purpose code 'Trade settlement – dropshipping inventory'. For high-value transactions (typically > C$100,000), a Documentary Letter of Credit (Commercial LC, UCP600) issued by the Canadian bank can be used to secure supplier payment, especially with Asian manufacturers. Alternatively, CAD clearing can be executed via the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) for same-day domestic settlement or via the Real-Time Rail (RTR) for retail payments. International disbursements must be screened against OFAC/UN/EU sanctions. No export surrender requirement applies; foreign currency settlement (USD/EUR) may be held in the operating account to optimize FX spread.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contracts (USD/CAD) with a Canadian Schedule I bank counterparty
FX swaps (swap CAD into USD and vice versa) for temporary liquidity management
Currency swaps for larger, multi-year liabilities (interest rate plus FX)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) are not typically necessary or permissible for CAD, as CAD is fully convertible; OSFI-regulated banks usually transact only deliverable forwards for CAD
Cross-currency basis swaps for foreign currency debt/working capital lines
FX options (call/put) on USD/CAD for downside protection, subject to bank approval and transaction reporting thresholds

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the corporation's incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to $500; company may be struck off the register after default notice and non-compliance period

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for distributing corporations or if required by articles of incorporation; generally not required for private corporations

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No mandatory annual confirmation for shareholding transfers; beneficial ownership information must be updated upon any changes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: N/A for private corporations; $2,000 - $8,000 if audit required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general headline (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%); an eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) applies a 12.2% combined rate on the first C$500,000 of qualifying active business income (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD) caps the first C$500,000 of qualifying Quebec active business income at the reduced CCPC rates; Quebec reduced corporate rate of 3.2% for eligible SMEs; refundable SR&ED investment tax credits (35% on qualified digital/R&D expenditures) may reduce effective cash tax; no sector-specific e-commerce tax holiday exists in Canada or Quebec

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) via Corporation Internet Filing / EFILE; supporting schedules (Schedule 1, Schedule 100) transmitted electronically in the same package
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 must be filed within 6 months after the fiscal period end; final balance of federal tax is due within 2 months after year-end (non-CCPC) or 3 months after year-end (CCPC); quarterly instalments become mandatory when tax payable exceeds C$3,000

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, CRA business number (BN) and income tax account, fiscal year start and end dates, jurisdiction of incorporation (Canada or Quebec), and type of corporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The target CA_CORP is Canadian-resident; non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada through a permanent establishment also file T2 and report only Canadian-source PE income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total worldwide gross revenue from all sources, including gross sales processed through Stripe/PayPal and automated dropshipping platforms, before payment-processor and supplier fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident reporting is limited to revenue attributable to the Canadian permanent establishment; payments received abroad for Canadian sales may still be taxable under Part I

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net income or loss adjusted to tax basis: add back amortization, non-deductible 50% meals/entertainment, non-deductible foreign taxes, and improperly deducted transactions; deduct eligible capital cost allowances and loss carryforwards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same reconciliation to Canadian PE books only; intercompany management/fee charges must meet arm's length transfer pricing standards

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after application of non-capital loss carryforwards and the SBD computation (Schedule 1); active business income of a CCPC up to C$500,000 is taxed at the reduced 9% federal rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned Canadian corporation cannot claim SBD; income allocated to a Quebec permanent establishment is reported on both federal and Quebec returns

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 400 / Line 700 - Base tax and total tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal base tax computed at the general rate and reduced SBD rate, less investment tax credits; total tax is reduced by foreign tax credits for U.S. or other-source withholding
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident payers may claim only limited credits; treaty benefits with respect to Canadian-source income are reflected in the T2 computation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net federal tax payable after deducting instalments paid during the year, including the Part I tax reconciliation and any Part XIII.1 tax on dividends
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, the balance due is due 2 months after year-end, with no CCPC extension; failure to remit triggers interest and director liability

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under s.162(1) is 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delay up to 12 months; repeat failure attracts an additional penalty under s.162(7.01); daily compound interest accrues at the CRA prescribed rate; failure to file supporting T5/NR4 information slips attracts per-slip penalties

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: CO-17 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed with Revenu Quebec via eTransmission / Transmission electronique de la TD4 (Quebec corporate tax software)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: CO-17 must be filed within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; the Quebec tax balance is due within 2 months after year-end for a non-CCPC and 3 months after year-end for an eligible CCPC; Quebec instalments are required when the prior year tax payable exceeds C$3,000

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), CRA business number, legal form, fiscal period, and place of incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Quebec file only if a Quebec permanent establishment (QPE) exists; the CO-17 must be completed even if the T2 reports no QPE

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 - Income from an enterprise carried on in Quebec
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenue allocated to the Quebec permanent establishment, including automated dropshipping sales to Quebec customers where servers/inventory/employees create a QPE
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-controlled dropshipping enterprise with Quebec warehouse or employee agency at risk of a QPE must allocate income on a formulaic basis

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 15 - Active business income and SBD computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the Quebec small business deduction, applying the 3.2% reduced rate to the first C$500,000 of eligible active business income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only a Canadian-controlled private corporation resident in Canada qualifies; a foreign-controlled enterprise is taxed at the general Quebec rate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec taxable income after loss carryforwards and Quebec-specific adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Quebec applies its own loss carryforward rules; the same federal-law loss chronology is generally respected

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Lines 36 to 60 - Tax before credits and balance due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computed at the general/reduced rates, less Quebec tax credits and instalments, leaving the net balance remitted to Revenu Quebec
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Instalments for non-residents are due quarterly without the CCPC extension

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Revenu Quebec imposes a late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months, daily interest, and specific penalties for failure to transmit T5/Releve 23 information; officers and directors are jointly liable for unremitted Quebec tax under the Tax Administration Act
